subject: physics
title: Lenses
key_idea: (Separate science) A lens forms an image by refracting light. A convex lens brings parallel rays to a principal focus and can make real or virtual images. A concave lens always makes a virtual image. Magnification = image height ÷ object height.

blocks.text: (Separate science) This section covers how lenses bend light and the key words for ray diagrams.

items.meaning: A piece of transparent material that forms an image by refracting light.
The point where parallel rays of light are brought together by a convex lens.
The distance from the lens to the principal focus.

rows: Brought together at the principal focus

items: A convex lens is drawn as a line with outward arrowheads.
A concave lens is drawn as a line with inward arrowheads.
Ray diagrams show the rays from an object, refracted by the lens, forming an image.
A ray parallel to the axis of a convex lens is refracted through the principal focus.
A ray through the centre of a lens carries straight on.
A ray parallel to the axis of a concave lens is refracted so it seems to come from the principal focus.
(Separate science) A convex lens brings parallel rays to a focus at the principal focus.
The focal length is the distance from the lens to the principal focus.
A concave lens spreads parallel rays out.

blocks.text: (Separate science) This section covers the two kinds of image a lens can make.

items.meaning: Formed where light rays actually meet. It can be caught on a screen.
Formed where light rays only appear to come from. It cannot be caught on a screen.

items: A convex lens can form a real image or a virtual image.
A convex lens used as a magnifying glass forms a magnified, upright, virtual image.
A concave lens always forms a virtual image.
A convex lens forms a real image when the object is further from the lens than the principal focus.
A convex lens forms a virtual image when the object is closer to the lens than the principal focus.
The image from a concave lens is upright and virtual.
To correct long sight, a convex lens refracts light inwards so that it focuses on the retina.
(Separate science) A convex lens can make real or virtual images.
A concave lens always makes an upright, virtual image.
A magnifying glass is a convex lens making a virtual image.

blocks.text: (Separate science) This section covers how to calculate the magnification of a lens.

blocks.label: Magnification
where: magnification has no unit because it is a ratio.
image height is in millimetres (mm) or centimetres (cm).
object height is in the same unit as the image height.

items: Use the same unit for both heights, either mm or cm.
Rearrange to find a height: image height = magnification × object height, and object height = image height ÷ magnification.

items.text: An image 12 mm high with magnification 4: object height = 12 ÷ 4 = 3 mm

diagram.alt: Calculate the image height from the object height and the magnification.
diagram.question: A lens has a magnification of {M}. The object is {h} mm high. Calculate the height of the image in mm.

items: magnification = image height ÷ object height.
Magnification has no unit.
Use the same unit for the image height and the object height.

checks.q: Which two words describe the image formed by a concave lens?
The image of a coin letter is 9.0 mm high and the magnification is 6.0. Calculate the height of the letter.
State what happens to rays of light parallel to the axis when they pass through a convex lens.
checks.a: They are refracted and brought together at the principal focus.

worked_example.question:
A person uses a lens to read the letters on the back of a coin.

The image height of the letters on the coin is 9.0 mm.

The magnification produced by the lens is 6.0.

Calculate the height of the letters on the coin.
worked_example.tip: An answer of 1.5 mm scores all 3 marks. The equation is on the equation sheet, so you do not need to remember it, but you do need to rearrange it.

worked_example.question:
A converging lens has a focal length of 40 cm.

Calculate the power of this lens in dioptres.

Use the equation

power in dioptres = 1 / focal length in metres
worked_example.tip: One mark for the substitution, one for the evaluation and one for including the unit change. A correct answer with no working scores full marks.

blocks.text: (Separate science) The power of a lens tells you how strongly it bends light.

items: A lens with a shorter focal length has a higher power.
A fatter, thicker, more curved lens has a shorter focal length and a higher power.
Converging lenses are convex and diverging lenses are concave.

diagram.alt: Change the focal length of a lens and see its power.

items: (Separate science) power = 1 ÷ focal length, with the focal length in metres.
A shorter focal length gives a higher power.
To make an image of a window on paper, place the paper behind the lens, with the window light on the other side.
Move the lens or the paper until the image is clear.
To increase magnification, use a lens of higher power, or change the distance between the object and the lens.

worked_example.question:
Lenses can be used to help people see clearly.

Explain how a convex lens can correct long-sighted vision.
answer_points: In long sight the rays are focused behind the retina (eyeball).
A convex lens refracts the light inwards, so it focuses on the retina.
worked_example.tip: A near object focused behind the retina, or an eyeball that is too short, is also accepted for the first mark.

worked_example.question:
The lens in a magnifying glass is a converging lens.

Converging lenses are used in spectacles (glasses) to correct one problem with vision.

State the name of the problem and explain how a converging lens is used to correct it.
answer_points: The converging lens moves the image towards the lens and the retina (it shortens the focal length of the combined lens).
It focuses the image on the retina (back of the eye).
worked_example.tip: One mark for the name and two marks for the explanation.

items.meaning: The line through the centre of the lens, at right angles to it. Parallel rays travel along it or parallel to it.
Formed where diverging rays seem to come from when they are extended backwards. It cannot be shown on a screen.

blocks.text: F is the principal focus. 2F is twice the focal length from the lens. The image from a convex lens depends on where the object is.

items.text: From the top of the object, draw a ray parallel to the principal axis. The lens refracts it through the principal focus.
From the top of the object, draw a ray through the centre of the lens. It carries straight on.
Where the two refracted rays cross is the top of the image. Draw the image from the principal axis up to that point.
If the object is closer than F, the rays spread out after the lens. Extend them backwards with dotted lines. They meet at the top of the virtual image.

blocks.text: A short-sighted eye focuses distant objects in front of the retina.

items: A concave (diverging) lens spreads the rays out slightly before they enter the eye.
The image then forms on the retina.
Long sight is corrected with a convex lens and short sight with a concave lens.
